messages:
Elaine (AE): HelixPay emailed: they want a single ZIP for the RFI bundle. Requirements: BOM (recommended sizing), POC per-hour cost estimate, filled security questionnaire, signed NDA link, SOW template, and a short capability matrix. Deadline: EOD tomorrow. Can we assemble? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Sam (Solutions Eng): Got it. What perf targets are they asking for?
Elaine (AE): Their technical lead wrote: "Service must sustain 150 embedding req/s with 99th latency < 200ms and p95 gen latency <= 1.2s at 2k tokens. Prefer VPC/private but will consider hosted w/ contractual commitments."
Priya (Solutions): I'll model two cost scenarios: 1) Private (dedicated) footprint, 2) Hosted with reserved baseline + burst. Token assumption I'll use: 2k tokens/session, 500 sessions/day, cache hit 40%.
Sam (Solutions Eng): OK. I'll run an AM microbenchmark on a small cluster. ops-bot, spin up 3xA100-sim nodes in us-east-1 for 2h labeled helixpay-poc-test.
ops-bot: Provisioning started. Request #INC-9017. ETA ~10m.
Sam (Solutions Eng): Planning to test both: embeddings load (200 users headless) and generation with 2k tokens. Will include the exact loadgen commands in the perf note.
Sam (Solutions Eng): Example commands I'll include:
```bash
# generation smoke (gen-2k tokens)
python perf/run_gen.py --model rwd-gen-2 --tokens 2000 --concurrency 20 --duration 5m
# embeddings quickload
locust -f perf/locust_embeddings.py --headless -u 200 -r 20 --run-time 5m
```
Priya (Solutions): For BOM I'll propose:
- Option Dedicated: 6xA100, control-plane 32 vCPU/128GB, 2TB NVMe, 99.95% SLA, enterprise support 24x7.
- Option Hosted-reserve+burst: 3xA100 reserved + autoscale to 12xA100 burst, lower baseline cost but higher peak egress and burst pricing.
Priya (Solutions): I'll produce a per-hour calculator using their workload assumptions and include a pre-filled sheet.
Elaine (AE): They also care about KMS and HSM. Jordan, can we export the standard KMS/HSM boilerplate and a DPA pointer?
Jordan (Legal): Will attach: "nda-signed-link.txt" (we'll provide a signed NDA link after receipt), "dpa-summary.txt", and a short KMS statement. Note: for POCs we remove broad indemnity and shorten obligation windows.
Priya (Solutions): Security questionnaire is 82 Qs. I've prefilled obvious low-risk answers and flagged 9 Qs as "requires legal/infrastructure input" (data retention, cross-region replication, HSM custody, disaster recovery RTO).
Jordan (Legal): For HSM: we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure). For Private we can integrate with on-prem HSMs (YubiHSM/Thales) — I'll add the caveat about provisioning lead time and runbook.
Sam (Solutions Eng): Important: add tech note on fallback determinism. I'll write: "Routing policy: prefer pinned model -> if pinned unavailable, attempt same-arch quantized replica -> if capacity still constrained, fallback to compatible hosted-llm with explict latency SLA; all fallbacks logged and tracing id returned."
Priya (Solutions): Also adding acceptance criteria for the POC:
- Throughput: 150 embeddings/s sustained over 10 minutes
- Gen latency: p95 <=1.2s at 2k tokens for 95% of traffic
- Data isolation: all request logs encrypted with customer key
- Support: 4hr on-call response during POC window
Elaine (AE): Good call. Buyer asked about logs/retention and audit access. Include short note: we can provide redacted request logs for the POC and SOC2 report excerpt.
Priya (Solutions): List of files I'll package into the ZIP:
[bom-dedicated-vs-burst.csv, poc-cost-calculator-filled.xlsx, security-answers-highrisk.pdf, redacted-network-diagram.png, kms-hsm-statement.txt, dpa-summary.txt, nda-conditional-link.txt, poc-sow-template.docx, perf-runbook.md, perf-results-snapshot.csv]
Sam (Solutions Eng): I'll attach perf-results-snapshot.csv and the raw command lines. Also will include a small script they can run to reproduce results (perf/repro.sh).
Jordan (Legal): NDA link uploaded to Drive; SOW template attached. Note: we should explicitly call out data deletion steps after POC in the SOW appendix.
Elaine (AE): Timeline: Priya + Sam finalize docs by 15:00 today, Jordan provides legal attachments by 17:00, I assemble ZIP and upload to Sales Drive by 18:30, then I send to buyer tomorrow morning with signed NDA.
Priya (Solutions): A couple of clarifications for the RFI matrix: do we list quantization levels (8-bit vs 4-bit) as supported or only recommend 8-bit for parity?
Sam (Solutions Eng): We support both but call out tradeoffs: 8-bit recommended for latency parity; 4-bit gains in cost but needs validation for specific model families. I'll add a small table mapping model family -> recommended quantization.
Elaine (AE): Awesome. If anything blocks, mention it here or DM me. Thanks team :raised_hands:
